facts.statement: Falcatus lived during the early Carboniferous Period in Bear Gulch Bay, now located in Montana.
facts.quote: Falcatus is an extinct genus of falcatid chondrichthyan which lived during the early Carboniferous Period in Bear Gulch bay in what is now Montana.

facts.statement: The species was originally described in 1883 from the St. Louis Limestone under the name Physonemus falcatus.
facts.quote: When first described in 1883 from the St. Louis Limestone, these remains were given the name Physonemus falcatus.

facts.statement: In 1985, fossils from Montana were described that revealed a high degree of sexual dimorphism in the genus.
facts.quote: However, in 1985, fossils of a new type of chondrichthyan from Montana were described that displayed a high degree of sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Falcatus was a small fish that grew to a length of 25 to 30 cm (10 to 12 inches).
facts.quote: This fish was quite small, only getting to around 25–30 cm or 10-12 inches long.

facts.statement: The genus is primarily known from prominent fin spines that curve forward over the animal's head.
facts.quote: The first material known from the genus were the prominent fin spines that curve anteriorly over the head of the animal.

facts.statement: Males possessed a prominent dorsal fin spine covered in denticles that curved over the head, while females lacked these spines and denticles.
facts.quote: Mostraban un fuerte dimorfismo sexual; los machos poseían una prominente espina en la primera aleta dorsal que se curvaban hacia adelante sobre la cabeza, que tenían cubierta de dentículos, mientras que las hembras carecía de espina y de dentículos cefálicos.

facts.statement: Falcatus was a predator that fed on shrimp.
facts.quote: Eran depredadores y se alimentaba de gambas.

facts.statement: Fossils of Falcatus have been found in Montana and Missouri, USA.
facts.quote: Falcatus es un género extinto de peces cartilaginosos del orden Symmoriida que vivieron en el Carbonífero Inferior, hace 335-318 millones de años; sus fósiles se han hallado en Montana y Misuri (Estados Unidos).

facts.statement: Falcatus lived between 330.3 and 323.4 million years ago during the Serpukhovian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Serpukhovian to Serpukhovian (330.3 to 323.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Many Falcatus fossils show distended gills, suggesting they died from asphyxiation in oxygen-poor waters.
facts.quote: However, because many of the fish fossils were found with distended gills, this would suggest death by asphyxiation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Falcatus died from asphyxiation in oxygen-poor waters or was rapidly buried by mudslides caused by heavy rainfall.
facts.quote: One is that the creatures sank to the bottom and died of asphyxiation in the oxygen poor waters, being preserved without scavenging took place. Another theory is that the bottom of the bay created mudslides because of heavy rainfall, which rapidly buried the creatures.

rejected.statement: Falcatus belongs to the order Symmoriiformes and subclass Holocephali, making it more closely related to chimaeras than to true sharks.
rejected.quote: Despite often being called a shark, Falcatus and its relatives were part of the order Symmoriiformes, which itself was part of the subclass Holocephali.
